original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Sharp integer-rank cost-alphabet screening for replacing k of the selected local word's 2412 rank-one children by blocks of rank 2..B, B=2..51, retaining all other local costs and old idle mass. Charge added work on top; determine the 5%-above-baseline primitive-ceiling threshold and the one-added-call-per-block obstruction.
scope_change_reason: The session completes the card's first optimistic budget experiment rather than synthesizing a physical decoder or proving which block ranks it can realize. The arbitrary integer block alphabet is an explicitly favorable relaxation; passing it does not satisfy the construction acceptance gate.
bottleneck_link: Rank-one children dominate much of the binding complex recursion cost. A sharp partial-reblocking and overhead budget tells a proposed block decoder how much extra copy/restoration work it can afford before synthesis.
stop_rule: Stop after all 50 block caps, sharp adjacent threshold signs, overhead bills, the 1/99 obstruction and source/receipt controls. Do not synthesize a new supplier or extend the alphabet.
evidence: RESULT.json: rank16 minimum 363/2412; full rank16 reblocking permits at most 10 added rank units; one added rank1 call per output block precludes any local payload-cost improvement at a<=target for every rank2..51; 10274 partition fixtures and 8 mathematical controls.
author: Arham Tahir
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in choosing the scope, proving the cost inequalities, implementing both interval methods, verification and documentation; no subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can a concrete rank16 block decoder combine at least 363 rank-one payload units with fewer than one added paid call per output block?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cost gate admits zero added rank1 calls at the first threshold and only ten added rank units after complete reblocking. Naive per-block overhead fails.
open_questions.first_step: Select one actual chronological climb group, pin its labels and source/target frames, and exhibit a dirty-state identity plus its gathering/restoration profile. Compare its complete additional invoice against the budget in RESULT.json.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical block-decoder realization or free gathering contract is supplied here.

open_questions.question: What overhead budget remains if rank2/rank3 children also change, or if the centre path is shared?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Rank-one reblocking alone cannot reach a=1/99 even at maximum block rank51. Another paid component must change.
open_questions.first_step: Derive the completed replacement profile and applicable coverage identity; add its full additional-work moment before checking an optimistic ceiling.
open_questions.blocked_by: New local-word/centre realization and inherited supplier interfaces require separate proofs.
